title: common
description: Definitions shared across contracts. This file describes no instance on its own; other schemas reference its definitions.

absPath.description: An absolute path without a trailing slash and without parent segments. Shape only: whether a path is within an account's reach is policy's answer, computed by the server from the composed fragments.

policyPath.description: A path a `files_read` or `files_write` entry names: an absolute path, or a path under the acting account's home written from its directory — `$HOME` for the home itself, `$HOME/Documents` for a folder in it, `$HOME/projects/neuman` for something deeper. The token is the spelling to prefer whenever the client may not be on the server's machine: it names the home of whichever machine runs the tool, which the client reports, while an absolute path names one machine's directory (N145). It also keeps a role valid across operating systems, where the home is `/home/<user>` or `/Users/<user>`. The bare token means the home whole, dotfiles included; a grant that wants particular folders names them (D105, D106).

machineLabel.description: A machine's name, within one account. The label is the machine's identity: a branch names it, policy grants it, the record carries it, and a client says it at the handshake. Scoped to an account rather than global, because reach differs per person: Alice's `dgx` and Bob's `dgx` are the same physical box and two different machines. Lower case because people type it and strings compare it, and a name differing only in case would be two machines or one depending on who is asking.

network.description: Whether the layer grants the network. `none` withholds every tool declaring `needs = ["network"]`; `any` admits them; null inherits. There is no host list: those tools run on the acting user's own machine over their network, so Neuman cannot narrow where they connect, and a list nothing enforced would read as a control that does not exist (N146).
